title_en: Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Exchange Control

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of strengthening foreign exchange administration, promoting equilibrium in the balance of payments, and facilitating the healthy development of the national economy.

Article 2 The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council and its branches (hereinafter collectively referred to as the foreign exchange administration authorities) shall perform their duties of foreign exchange administration according to law and shall be responsible for the implementation of these Regulations.

Article 4 These Regulations shall apply to the foreign exchange receipts and payments or foreign exchange business activities of domestic institutions and domestic individuals, as well as the foreign exchange receipts and payments or foreign exchange business activities of overseas institutions and overseas individuals within the territory of China.
Article 5 The State shall not impose restrictions on current international payments and transfers.

Article 6 The State shall practice a system of statistical declaration for the balance of payments.
The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council shall conduct statistics and monitoring of the balance of payments, and shall regularly publish the status of the balance of payments.

Article 7 Financial institutions engaged in foreign exchange business shall, in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council, open foreign exchange accounts for customers and handle foreign exchange business through such accounts.
Financial institutions engaged in foreign exchange business shall, according to law, report to the foreign exchange administration authorities the foreign exchange receipts and payments of customers and changes in their accounts.

Article 8 Within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the circulation of foreign currency is prohibited, and it shall not be used for pricing or settlement, unless otherwise provided by the State.

Article 9 Foreign exchange income of domestic institutions and domestic individuals may be repatriated to China or deposited overseas; the conditions and time limits for repatriation or overseas deposit shall be prescribed by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council in accordance with the balance of payments situation and the needs of foreign exchange administration.

Article 10 The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council shall, according to law, hold, manage and operate the state foreign exchange reserves, following the principles of safety, liquidity and value preservation.

Article 11 When the balance of payments is or may be in serious disequilibrium, or when the national economy is or may be in serious crisis, the State may take necessary safeguard and control measures with respect to the balance of payments.

Article 12 Foreign exchange receipts and payments under the current account shall have a genuine and lawful transaction basis. Financial institutions engaged in the business of exchange settlement and sale shall, in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council, conduct reasonable review of the authenticity of transaction documents and their consistency with foreign exchange receipts and payments.
The foreign exchange administration authorities shall have the power to supervise and inspect the matters specified in the preceding paragraph.

Article 13 Foreign exchange income under the current account may be retained or sold to financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 14 Foreign exchange expenditures under the current account shall, in accordance with the administrative provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council on payment and purchase of foreign exchange, be paid with self-owned foreign exchange or by purchasing foreign exchange from financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business against valid documents.

Article 15 The limits for carrying and declaring foreign currency cash into and out of the territory of China shall be prescribed by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.

Article 16 Where an overseas institution or overseas individual makes direct investment in China, it/he shall, after obtaining approval from the relevant competent authority, register with the foreign exchange administration authorities.
Where an overseas institution or overseas individual engages in the issuance or trading of securities or derivatives in China, it/he shall comply with the State provisions on market access, and shall register in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.

Article 17 Where a domestic institution or domestic individual makes outward direct investment or engages in the issuance or trading of overseas securities or derivatives, it/he shall register in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council. Where the State requires prior approval or filing with the relevant competent authority, the procedures for approval or filing shall be completed before the foreign exchange registration.

Article 18 The State shall practice scale management of external debt. Borrowing external debt shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, and the external debt shall be registered with the foreign exchange administration authorities.
The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council shall be responsible for the statistics and monitoring of the national external debt, and shall regularly publish the status of external debt.

Article 19 To provide an outward guarantee, an application shall be submitted to the foreign exchange administration authorities, and the foreign exchange administration authorities shall make a decision to approve or disapprove based on the applicant's assets and liabilities, etc.; where the State provides that the applicant's business scope requires approval from the relevant competent authority, the approval procedures shall be completed before submitting the application to the foreign exchange administration authorities. After the applicant signs an outward guarantee contract, it shall register the outward guarantee with the foreign exchange administration authorities.
Where an outward guarantee is provided with the approval of the State Council for the purpose of on-lending loans from foreign governments or international financial organizations, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall not apply.

Article 20 Banking financial institutions may directly provide commercial loans to overseas parties within their approved business scope. Other domestic institutions that provide commercial loans to overseas parties shall submit an application to the foreign exchange administration authorities, and the foreign exchange administration authorities shall make a decision to approve or disapprove based on the applicant's assets and liabilities, etc.; where the State provides that the applicant's business scope requires approval from the relevant competent authority, the approval procedures shall be completed before submitting the application to the foreign exchange administration authorities.
Where commercial loans are provided to overseas parties, registration shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.

Article 21 The retention of foreign exchange income under the capital account or the sale of such income to financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business shall be subject to approval by the foreign exchange administration authorities, unless the State provides that approval is not required.

Article 22 Foreign exchange expenditures under the capital account shall, in accordance with the administrative provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council on payment and purchase of foreign exchange, be paid with self-owned foreign exchange or by purchasing foreign exchange from financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business against valid documents. Where the State provides that approval by the foreign exchange administration authorities is required, the approval procedures shall be completed before the foreign exchange payment.
For an enterprise with foreign investment that is terminated according to law, after liquidation and payment of taxes in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, the Renminbi belonging to the foreign investor may be converted into foreign exchange and remitted abroad through purchase from financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business.

Article 23 Foreign exchange under the capital account and the funds settled shall be used for the purposes approved by the relevant competent authorities and the foreign exchange administration authorities. The foreign exchange administration authorities shall have the power to supervise and inspect the use of foreign exchange under the capital account and the settled funds, as well as changes in accounts.

Article 24 Where a financial institution engages in or terminates the business of exchange settlement and sale, it shall obtain approval from the foreign exchange administration authorities; where it engages in or terminates other foreign exchange businesses, it shall, in accordance with the division of responsibilities, obtain approval from the foreign exchange administration authorities or the financial regulatory agency.

Article 25 The foreign exchange administration authorities shall practice comprehensive position management over the foreign exchange businesses of financial institutions, and the specific measures shall be formulated by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.

Article 26 Where a financial institution needs to convert between Renminbi and foreign currencies due to its capital, profits or mismatch between domestic and foreign currency assets, it shall obtain approval from the foreign exchange administration authorities.
Article 27 A managed floating exchange rate system based on market supply and demand shall be practiced for the Renminbi exchange rate.

Article 28 Financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business and other institutions that meet the conditions prescribed by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council may conduct foreign exchange transactions in the inter-bank foreign exchange market in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.
Article 29 Transactions in the foreign exchange market shall follow the principles of openness, fairness, impartiality and good faith.
Article 30 The currencies and forms of transactions in the foreign exchange market shall be prescribed by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.
Article 31 The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council shall, according to law, supervise and administer the national foreign exchange market.

Article 32 The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council may, in accordance with changes in the foreign exchange market and the requirements of monetary policy, regulate the foreign exchange market according to law.

Article 34 When foreign exchange administration authorities conduct supervision and inspection or investigation according to law, the number of personnel conducting such supervision and inspection or investigation shall be no less than two, and they shall produce their credentials. Where the number of personnel conducting supervision, inspection or investigation is less than two or they fail to produce their credentials, the units and individuals under supervision, inspection or investigation shall have the right to refuse.

Article 35 Domestic institutions engaged in foreign exchange business activities shall, in accordance with the provisions of the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council, submit financial accounting reports, statistical statements and other materials.

Article 36 Where a financial institution engaged in foreign exchange business discovers that a customer has committed an illegal foreign exchange act, it shall promptly report to the foreign exchange administration authorities.

Article 37 For the purpose of performing its foreign exchange administration duties, the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council may obtain necessary information from the relevant departments and agencies of the State Council, and such departments and agencies shall provide such information.
The foreign exchange administration department of the State Council shall notify the relevant departments and agencies of the State Council of the status of foreign exchange administration work.

Article 38 Any unit or individual shall have the right to report illegal foreign exchange acts.
The foreign exchange administration authorities shall keep the confidentiality of the informants, and shall, in accordance with the provisions, give rewards to the informants or the units and individuals that have rendered meritorious service in assisting in the investigation and handling of illegal foreign exchange acts.

Article 39 Where any person commits an act of foreign exchange evasion such as illegally transferring foreign exchange from within the territory to overseas, or transferring domestic capital overseas by means of deception, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order the person to repatriate the foreign exchange within a specified time limit and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the amount of foreign exchange evaded; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than the equivalent amount of the foreign exchange evaded shall be imposed; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 40 Where any person commits an act of illegal arbitrage such as illegally receiving or paying in foreign exchange amounts that shall be received or paid in Renminbi, or fraudulently purchasing foreign exchange from financial institutions engaged in exchange settlement and sale business using false or invalid transaction documents, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order the person to reconvert the illegally arbitraged funds, and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the amount of illegal arbitrage; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than the equivalent amount of the illegal arbitrage shall be imposed; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 41 Where any person remits foreign exchange into the territory of China in violation of the provisions, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order rectification and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the illegal amount; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than the equivalent amount of the illegal amount shall be imposed.
Where any person illegally settles foreign exchange, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order the person to reconvert the illegally settled funds, and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the illegal amount.

Article 42 Where any person carries foreign exchange into or out of the territory in violation of the provisions, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall give a warning and may impose a fine of not more than 20% of the illegal amount. Where the laws and administrative regulations provide that the Customs shall impose a penalty, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 43 Where any person commits an act violating the administration of external debt, such as unauthorized external borrowing, issuance of bonds abroad, or provision of outward guarantees, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall give a warning and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the illegal amount.

Article 44 Where any person, in violation of the provisions, unauthorizedly changes the purpose of use of foreign exchange or settled funds, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order rectification, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the illegal amount; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than the equivalent amount of the illegal amount shall be imposed.
Where any person commits an act of illegal use of foreign exchange such as pricing or settlement in foreign currency within the territory, or transferring foreign exchange in violation of the provisions, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order rectification, give a warning, and may impose a fine of not more than 30% of the illegal amount.

Article 45 Where any person privately buys or sells foreign exchange, buys or sells foreign exchange in a disguised form, scalps foreign exchange, or illegally introduces the buying or selling of foreign exchange in a relatively large amount, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall give a warning, confiscate the illegal gains, and impose a fine of not more than 30% of the illegal amount; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than the equivalent amount of the illegal amount shall be imposed; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 46 Where any person engages in exchange settlement and sale business without approval, the foreign exchange administration authorities shall order rectification; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated, and if the illegal gains are 500,000 yuan or more, a fine of not less than one time but not more than five times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if there are no illegal gains or the illegal gains are less than 500,000 yuan, a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2 million yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the relevant competent authority shall order suspension of business for rectification or revoke the business permit; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Where any person engages in foreign exchange businesses other than exchange settlement and sale without approval, the foreign exchange administration authorities or the financial regulatory agency shall impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph.

Article 49 Where a domestic institution violates the provisions on foreign exchange administration, in addition to the penalties imposed in accordance with these Regulations, the persons directly in charge and other persons directly responsible shall be given sanctions; the directors, supervisors, senior officers and other persons directly responsible of a financial institution shall be given a warning and a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 50 Where any staff member of the foreign exchange administration authorities engages in graft, abuse of power or dereliction of duty, if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law; if no crime is constituted, an administrative sanction shall be imposed according to law.

Article 51 If a party refuses to accept the specific administrative act made by the foreign exchange administration authority, it may apply for administrative reconsideration according to law; if it is still not satisfied with the reconsideration decision, it may bring an administrative action in the People's Court according to law.

Article 52 For the purpose of these Regulations, the meanings of the following terms are:
(1) Domestic institutions refer to state organs, enterprises, institutions, social organizations, military units, etc. within the territory of the People's Republic of China, excluding foreign diplomatic and consular missions in China and representative offices of international organizations in China.
(2) Domestic individuals refer to Chinese citizens and foreigners who have resided continuously in the People's Republic of China for one full year, excluding foreign diplomatic personnel in China and representatives of international organizations in China.
(3) Current account items refer to transaction items involving goods, services, income and current transfers in the balance of payments, etc.
(4) Capital account items refer to transaction items that cause changes in the level of external assets and liabilities in the balance of payments, including capital transfers, direct investment, securities investment, derivative products and loans, etc.

Article 53 Non-financial institutions that conduct foreign exchange settlement and sale business shall be approved by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council, and specific administrative measures shall be formulated separately by the foreign exchange administration department of the State Council.
Article 54 These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
